title: Causes and Effects of the Industrial Revolution
question: Did the benefits of the Industrial Revolution outweigh the costs?

wynk.head: Where it starts
wynk.text: In 1750 most British people lived in the countryside, and many of them farmed. Villages shared open fields and common land. Wealthy landowners controlled Parliament, and looking for bigger profits they passed thousands of enclosure acts that fenced that land into private farms. New farming methods grew more food with fewer workers. Families who lost their land moved to the towns to look for work.

wynk.head: Why Britain first
wynk.text: Britain had coal, iron ore and rivers, ports and a navy that controlled the seas, people with money to invest, and more workers every year. In 1776 Adam Smith argued that splitting a job into small steps made workers far more productive, and that government should stay out of business.

wynk.head: What changed
wynk.text: Cloth had been made by hand at home. New machines sped it up, and James Watt's improved steam engine meant a mill no longer had to sit beside a fast river. Machines, a building and workers came together in one place: the factory. Canals and then railways made coal, cotton and finished goods cheaper to move.

wynk.head: What it cost
wynk.text: Cities grew faster than clean water, sewers and housing. Children worked long hours in dangerous places. People answered: Parliament's Factory Acts, labor unions, Robert Owen, Karl Marx.

wynk.head: What you will argue
wynk.text: Did the benefits of the Industrial Revolution outweigh the costs? You will need both sides, and the evidence for each.
